reviews.text:
My dog ​​had started eating less dry food, so I went to consult with them.

I tried the food they recommended, and to my surprise, he ate it with gusto, happily gobbling it up! 😊
They also showed me many venison treats, and he ate them all with such gusto that it made me happy just watching him.

The staff were very kind and explained everything thoroughly, which put me at ease.

The owner also explained each food item in detail, which made me realize how important daily food is for a dog to live a long and healthy life.

Of course, everyone has their own way of thinking, and some might consider my perspective biased.

But I felt a little ashamed of myself for thinking, "As long as he eats it, that's all that matters."

Because he's such a precious member of my family, I want to pay more attention to what he eats from now on.

I think this is a wonderful shop that truly cares about dogs.

I'd love to visit again for more advice! 🐶💕

I felt that everything was overpriced.

They charge for paper bags, and while I understand charging for a large bag is unavoidable, they charge 55 yen for a really flimsy bag. When I bought something slightly heavy, the bag ripped on the way home, which was a real hassle.

For 55 yen, I think they should provide a more decent paper bag. Also, I imagine some people give gifts, and you can't give something in a crumpled paper bag.

Another thing that bothered me was when a dog owner brought their dog in and, without saying anything, gave the dog treats and food while the owner was browsing the merchandise. What if the dog had an allergy?

What if the dog had a medical condition and it was something it shouldn't eat?

The thought of my beloved dog being treated like that sends shivers down my spine.

This shop had its own unique theories.

They were practically vegan.

They made statements that seemed to prioritize dogs, but I felt they were just trying to force their own theories on others.

What kind of outdated rumors are they taking seriously and lecturing customers from above? It was extremely unpleasant to listen to. A shop exists because of its customers; why would you intentionally make your customers uncomfortable?

The owner? The manager? As soon as we walked in, even though we were holding the leash short, she suddenly pulled on the leash and said, "No!" We go to a chiropractor, but she did something we never normally do, so we quickly picked her up. As soon as she sniffed the dog, she said, "It's for sale, so don't let it sniff!" I would understand if we were being persistent, but it was only a minute after we walked in, so I was really shocked! Are you the owner? Or the manager? If I had read the reviews beforehand, I probably wouldn't have gone. She seemed like a stubborn woman who wouldn't make any improvements, so I'm sure she doesn't care about bad rumors! I'm going to write a thorough review! I'm never going back! I don't even want to give it one star!

On Saturday afternoon, we went to George's to buy a leash for our Chihuahua. As soon as we entered the store, our Chihuahua started barking incessantly at other dogs and tried to bite the staff. My husband and I were about to leave when a staff member called us back to the back. There, we met the owner of George's. Our Chihuahua, who had been barking the whole time, suddenly stopped barking when the owner gave him a choker-style leash and a venison jerky on a towel on the grass.

Whenever the Chihuahua barked, the owner waved the choker, and he stopped barking instantly.

From then on, it was as if by magic; our Chihuahua became incredibly well-behaved.

Even on walks, our Chihuahua, who used to just look down, sniff everything, and bark incessantly at people and other dogs, stopped barking completely after putting on the choker and now walks right beside us!

There were mixed opinions and various comments in the reviews regarding the owner's philosophy, but George's owner is wonderful.

Dogs are intelligent. If we owners don't change our way of thinking, our dogs will continue to bark forever. I'm so grateful that we met George's owner at this time.

Now, George is growing up to be a smart dog, lying on a towel on the grass and eating venison jerky.

I visited the store because I was completely clueless about dog ownership and wanted to talk to someone knowledgeable.
I found much of what you said about dog relationships and training methods relatable and helpful.
However, you dragged my puppy, who wasn't used to the leash or collar, around the store quite forcefully.
He sat there with his tail tucked in, looking frightened and scared to us, but the saleswoman explained, "He's not scared, he trusts you!" Is that really true?

Without any explanation, you sprayed him with a strong-smelling insect repellent multiple times. It must have been quite frightening for him, because now he gets scared and runs away even at the slightest sound of spraying.

I think I'll never bring my dog ​​there again.
Please be careful of the short, high-pitched saleswoman.
The products they have in stock are very good, though.
They have cute patterned clothes, clothes that can help with the heat, and snacks that I think my child would like. I'd like to take my child with me next time.

They're a bit pricey, but they have stylish and highly functional products.

They also have a wide variety of reeds and other accessories.
I was interested in dog goods from overseas ♥️

First of all, the products are expensive, and they keep giving out samples without permission and then launching into sales pitches.
My dog ​​ate a deer bone with meat on it, and the next morning he had diarrhea and was diagnosed with colitis after a vet visit.
They suggested that it might have been because he ate something unfamiliar and the bone fragments irritated him, but I wish they would just stop giving him samples like they did before.
They are very pushy, and when I said I wouldn't buy anything this time, they suddenly became cold and dismissive, saying "Oh, really?" I will never go there again.
It was a shop with a dangerous, almost vegan-like ideology that went beyond mere love for dogs.

I visited "GEORGE OSAKA" in Higobashi. It's a stylish pet supply store with a striking blue awning and large logo. The store has high ceilings and a spacious feel, and it's a fun place to browse, with a wide variety of dog supplies including leashes, collars, clothes, and treats.

It's a little different from a typical mass-market store; it has more of a select shop atmosphere, with many highly designed items. They also have products for large dogs and unique items not commonly found elsewhere, so dog lovers will definitely enjoy it.

This time, my wife stopped by because she was worried about walking our dog, Vol de Wanwan. I was impressed by how the staff listened to her concerns and gave her advice. I've seen some harsh reviews online, but I felt that the staff were very helpful and attentive during our visit.

At the end, they said, "Please bring Wanwan next time!" Since our current leash is getting old, I'm planning to bring Wanwan next time to look at new leashes.


The prices are a little on the higher side, but considering the attention to detail in the space and the products, it's a shop that dog lovers should definitely check out at least once.

Pugs are currently banned worldwide, as are French Bulldogs and Bulldogs. Cavalier King Charles Spaniels are banned because breeding them is considered animal abuse.

Of course, this shop treats customers who bought their dogs from pet shops or breeders with respect.

The owner is still persevering despite the vastly different stances on dogs between Japan and San Francisco, where George's is located.

The uniforms worn by George's staff clearly state "Do not Breed" and "Do not Buy," and also feature the stylish phrase, "Whatever color the great artist made you, I like you just the way you are."

It's good to know the meaning of words like "puppy mill" before coming to this shop, but after reading other people's reviews, I can't help but think that Japan is really behind in animal welfare.

Keep up the good work, George.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Amazing! The staff and owner were so kind. They have a very cool selection of treats to take back to America. They also have quality outfits and collars.

Cool treats like horse and deer

I would not recommend this place to anyone who thinks of their dog as their own.

Like the others, they force unreasonable sales tactics and unintelligible theories on their dogs.

They seemed friendly throughout, but there were times when I felt annoyed.

When they brought out a treat and my dog ​​barked for it, they clicked their tongue (he doesn't normally bark that much).

They guided me elsewhere even though I only came to buy the item I wanted.

They didn't treat my dog ​​with the customer's perspective at all.

They also got my dog's name wrong at the end and didn't even apologize, which left me feeling sad.

I really don't recommend this place if you don't want your dog to be put through a tough experience.

Based on previous reviews, they haven't made any improvements to their training, and if you feel uncomfortable just going there,

I think you should buy from a different store.

By the way, contrary to appearances, leashes and other items wear out within a year of purchase.

I purchased four of them and almost all of them were the same, so please be aware of this.

You'll be served by an owner who doesn't understand human or dog feelings, and a kind but well-trained staff member.
As other reviews mention, my dog ​​was pulled hard on a short leash, lifted up loosely with one hand, and his eyes became bloodshot and one eye started to cross, which really worried me.
How long are they going to keep believing in willpower and mental fortitude?
Before talking about "what they do in America," they should update themselves first. They're completely stuck in the Showa era.
They should read more medical papers on pet animals.

Do the store staff even know how to handle dogs? They just came over and started touching my dog ​​without any permission, and then picked him up vertically by his sides without even supporting his rear end.

If they're selling dog supplies, I expect them to have some basic common sense.

My dog ​​has had a herniated disc before, so I never want to go back there again.
There's always something I like there. The staff are always smiling and teach me about dog food, training, and all sorts of other things. I've been going there for over 15 years.

I got a dog a few months ago and had been curious about this restaurant, so I finally got to go! 🩶
The female staff member was very enthusiastic and even let me try their venison and dog food! 🐶

This is my first time owning a dog, so I didn't know much about it, but they were so helpful! 🙏

Even though it was someone else's dog, they treated him with such love as if he were their own, which made me so happy! 😊💖 This restaurant is full of people who are incredibly affectionate towards animals!

Even though my dog ​​isn't very friendly with people, he was calm and calm, so I was relieved. ♡

This restaurant might not be for the pickiest people, but I recommend it to anyone who wants to improve their pet!

I thought it was just for dogs, but they also had cat food!

Thank you so much for the food samples! I want to go back soon! 🐶

My parents recommended this place, so I came all the way from Nagoya.

I had been worrying about training all day,
but the leash solved it all!!
The methods I learned have really helped me communicate with my dog.

They also taught me how to feed and drink in a way that's right for my dog.

Before, I was worried because he was so clingy that I had to be constantly with him and couldn't do anything else, but now that I'm more confident, my dog ​​is calm and well-behaved every day.

The water training clothes are also of very high quality, so I'm very satisfied!

I was surprised that my dog, who is shy and doesn't get close to anyone other than me, became so attached to the staff! I'll definitely visit again regularly!

Honestly great quality products and awesome service. Thank you very much for showing us how far developed pet products have become and your amazing inventory. Best wishes from Germany!!! We got a toy that transforms into other toys made out of wool :) our Labrador will love it for sure

I went to buy a collar and leash.

I went to have the collar size measured, but they just put the leash on my puppy without asking and dragged him around the store, even though he's only 3-4 months old.

Three different store employees took turns holding him and forcibly dragging him around.

They were pulling the leash upwards, dragging him, and it was choking him.

I felt so sorry for him that I snatched the leash from the employee and held it in front of his neck. When I walked, he walked properly with me.

Then the employee said, "Oh, you're so good!"

No. Isn't it obvious that a dog would hate being suddenly pulled in an uncomfortable position by someone they don't know?

They might think they're experienced, but it's the owner who understands their dog's habits, dislikes, and likes.

Seeing my dog ​​suffer broke my heart. When I picked him up on the way home, his eyes were bloodshot. I wish all the store employees would be suddenly dragged around by a stranger with a collar on.

Then, please consider the feelings of the dogs and their owners when serving customers. That's all.

Thank you as always 😊
You can learn about canine sociology.

They help my dog ​​practice walking on a leash.
When we get home, he's exhausted and sleeps soundly.
It's more like a training ground than a pet shop. …
This is the worst store. They have no love for pets. Of course, they have no consideration for the owners.
